checkpoints.title: Tradeoff duel
checkpoints.prompt: Fifty outlets publish the same story. What does the user see?

options.label: Show every article
options.verdict: The front page becomes fifty variations of one headline. The user's problem is not finding the news, it is that the same news arrives fifty times.

options.label: Cluster near-duplicates
options.verdict: Group articles covering the same event and surface one, with the rest available underneath. The unit of the product becomes the story rather than the article.

options.label: Threshold tuning between over- and under-merging
Latency between publication and cluster assignment
A choice of which article represents the cluster
The need to store fewer articles

defend.explain: You still store everything — clustering is a view over it. The costs are a similarity threshold that is never perfectly right, a delay before a new article joins its cluster, and an editorial choice about which source leads.

checkpoints.title: Capacity ladder
checkpoints.prompt: An aggregator that must stay fresh through breaking news.

rungs.q: What a breaking story does to ingest
choices: A sharp correlated spike across sources
rungs.note: Every outlet publishes within minutes of each other.

rungs.q: Acceptable delay before a story appears
rungs.note: Freshness is the product; an hour late is worthless.
Read-time clustering would put embedding and comparison on every page load.

checkpoints.explain: Breaking news is a correlated spike, not random load — which is precisely when the pipeline must not fall behind.

checkpoints.title: Architecture builder
checkpoints.prompt: Build the ingest path from feed to a clustered story.
checkpoints.explain: Polling, fetching and parsing produce article text; Kafka decouples that from the expensive embedding and clustering stages so a publication spike queues. Ranking and serving read from the story store — they are downstream of clustering, never inline with it.

checkpoints.title: Spot the bottleneck
checkpoints.prompt: Breaking stories appear 40 minutes late. Older stories are clustered correctly.
checkpoints.explain: The queue is deep because its consumer cannot drain it, and the consumer is pinned at 99% GPU. Embedding is the expensive stage and it has become the pipeline's throughput ceiling during a correlated spike. Batch embeddings, scale the GPU pool with queue depth, or run a cheap lexical pre-filter so only plausible near-duplicates need a vector.

wrong.Kafka: 900k lag is the backlog in front of the real constraint.
wrong.Story Store: Fast, and it is storing everything that reaches it.
wrong.Fetcher: Articles are being collected fine — they are stuck before clustering.
